clue.text: Restraint from some at business after re-organisation

indicators.note: once something has been re-organised its parts sit in a new order, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: all fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A company shows some restraint after a shake-up of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'some at business' is the fodder, all fourteen letters of ABSTEMIOUSNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemiousness is moderation in eating and drinking, a form of self-restraint.

clue.text: Full of excitement as case prepared for holiday

blocks.note: a legal case is an action in court
you have packed when your suitcase is ready for a trip

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled as their suitcase is ready for the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like the suitcase, but it is the lawsuit; the luggage only appears through 'prepared for holiday'.
explanation.definitionFit: An action-packed film or day is crammed with thrilling events, so it is full of excitement.

clue.text: Wasted pound found in street

indicators.note: something found in a place is sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen

explanation.surface: A pound coin turns up in the street, money thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests money or L, but here it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent and wasted both describe something used up or squandered, as in spent energy.

clue.text: Get rid of acid brought up: eater struggling to swallow it

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from the bottom, i.e. backwards
a struggling word is thrashing about, its letters thrown out of order
what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone with acid reflux tries to get rid of it, struggling to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the acid: the reversed acid goes inside the jumbled eater.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy or remove completely, i.e. get rid of.

clue.text: Rather concerned with terrible dates

indicators.note: terrible suggests something messed up, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: in means involved or concerned with, as in 'in property'
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worried by awful romantic dates would rather stay home.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead and rather both introduce a preferred alternative, as in 'tea instead of coffee'.

clue.text: Does crack? Bad luck, son

indicators.note: bad implies something gone wrong, so the letters following are disordered

explanation.surface: A parent asks whether their son takes drugs, then commiserates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son' is used whole here, not abbreviated: all seven letters of luck and son are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a safe or a code is to open it, so one who does crack unlocks.

clue.text: Cleanse a newborn's bottom going over the worst bit

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its final letter
going over in a down clue flips the run of letters so they read upwards

blocks.note: to rid is to clear or cleanse of something

explanation.surface: A parent changing a nappy finds cleaning the baby's bottom the worst part.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, so the worst bit of an experience.

clue.text: Bill to demonstrate locks on case: run through combinations

indicators.note: to lock something in is to hold it fast inside

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD for short
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A locksmith's bill for showing how the locks on a safe work, running through the codes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combinations' suggests safe codes; in boxing a combination is a sequence of punches practised against an imaginary opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow-box is to spar alone, practising sequences of punches without an opponent.

clue.text: Tip of triangle rotates at what angle, trigonometrically?

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter
turning something round brings its end to the front, so the following letters read backwards

blocks.note: eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: A geometry question: when a triangle's corner is turned, through what angle has it moved?
explanation.walkthrough: The setter later said 'rotates' should have read 'rotating'; the reversal applies to 'at what', not to the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the Greek letter conventionally used to label an unknown angle in trigonometry.

clue.text: Down pub drinking first couple of lagers – food served here

indicators.note: the first couple means the opening two letters of the word that follows
what is drunk goes inside the drinker

explanation.surface: Someone heads down the pub for a few lagers before eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction to the pub but means sad; the lager letters go inside sad only.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad bar is a counter in a restaurant where salads are served, often self-service.

clue.text: Place to take off sports kit after winning

blocks.note: landing a prize or a contract is winning it
a team's strip is its sports kit

explanation.surface: Players remove their kit in the changing room after a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests undressing; it is aircraft taking off. In Britain a team's strip is its uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a runway, a place where aircraft take off as well as land.

clue.text: Public calling for plan

blocks.note: news that is out is public
one's line of work is one's calling

explanation.surface: People call for a plan to be made public.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough plan or sketch of what is intended.

clue.text: Saloon, perhaps getting one local stripped for a Brazilian

indicators.note: stripped means its outer covering is removed, so both end letters go

blocks.note: a saloon is a type of car

explanation.surface: A saloon bar's regular strips off to get a Brazilian wax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' in British English is a four-door car, and also a bar; 'a Brazilian' plays on the waxing sense but means a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carioca is a native or inhabitant of Rio de Janeiro, so a Brazilian.

clue.text: Stages cricket match every year outside

indicators.note: one piece placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Organisers stage a cricket match every year outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia, plural of podium, are raised platforms, i.e. stages for speakers or winners.

clue.text: Fast motorbike maybe passing on corner?

blocks.note: passing is a euphemism for dying
to corner someone is to trap them; 'on' sets this piece after the first

explanation.surface: A speeding bike overtaking on a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' and 'corner' sound like road manoeuvres; one is death and the other a verb meaning trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is anything likely to kill its user, and a fast motorbike is offered as an example.

clue.text: Anxious bride going off with stud

indicators.note: going off means turning bad or exploding, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A nervous bride runs off with a handsome stud.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disturbed is to be troubled or worried, so anxious.

clue.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer supporting unqualified bankers in autumn statement

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its two edges, so only its outer letters are kept
in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, i.e. comes last

blocks.note: first and last letters of autumn

explanation.surface: The Chancellor's autumn budget backs bankers with no strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like UK fiscal news (the Chancellor is Britain's finance minister); 'bankers' means the two edge letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something spoken, a statement or remark.

clue.text: Persistent lawsuit about ecstasy going before bar

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
bar means except, as does less

explanation.surface: A lengthy drug case drags on before the bar of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests the legal profession, but here it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means never stopping, so persistent.

clue.text: Gut reaction, ultimately admit love at the start

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the preceding word, its final letter
these pieces are placed at the beginning, before the other one

blocks.note: to admit someone is to let them enter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An instinctive reaction, in the end, is to admit love early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gut reaction' reads as one phrase; split it, as 'Gut' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The enteron is the alimentary canal, the gut of an animal.

clue.text: Some in ISA to shift money for online investment

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone moves savings out of an ISA into crypto.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: A satoshi is the smallest unit of bitcoin, a digital currency invested in online.

clue.text: Against vote on ballot: surrounded by harmful material

blocks.note: to can mean against, as in 'ear to the wall'
a cross is the mark of a vote on a ballot paper
being in something means it surrounds you

explanation.surface: A voter opposes a ballot measure about hazardous substances.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison, a substance harmful to living things.

clue.text: Weary old American wearing hat

indicators.note: what is worn covers the wearer, so the hat goes around the other piece

explanation.surface: A tired old American in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weary' is a verb here: to exhaust someone is to weary them.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone is to tire them out completely, i.e. to weary them.

clue.text: Top protective equipment? Query oddly missing stocks

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters missing, only the even ones remain
a shop stocks goods, holding them inside

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of query

explanation.surface: A question about whether the protective gear is in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top protective equipment' reads as one phrase, but 'Top' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher or top, as in the upper deck.

clue.text: Dancing escort hugging hard: they get turned on in the dark

definitions.text: they get turned on in the dark

indicators.note: a dancer moves about, so the letters are moved into a new order
what hugs something has it wrapped inside

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dancing couple embrace tightly, getting aroused in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy definition is innocent: torches are switched on in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Torches are hand-held lights, switched on when it is dark.

clue.text: Irritation to be under husband's thumb

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece placed under another sits below it, so it comes second

explanation.surface: It is irritating to be under your husband's thumb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumb' is the verb, to hitch a lift, not the controlling husband's digit.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a ride and to hitch a ride both mean hitchhiking, signalling cars with the thumb.

clue.text: Gets ready: salesperson trims nails

indicators.note: to nail something is to pin it down and hold it fast, so the first piece is gripped inside

explanation.surface: A salesperson gets ready for a meeting by trimming their fingernails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trims nails' reads as manicure; the nails are the verb, holding the salesperson in.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepares means makes ready or gets ready.

clue.text: One marking last bit of paper after school returns

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word reads backwards
the last bit of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English school

explanation.surface: A teacher marks the last page of homework after school resumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an English private school, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A noter is one who notes or marks something down.

clue.text: Program on new tablet ultimately freezes in time

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the preceding word, its final letter

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
something in is fashionable, or hip

explanation.surface: An app on a new tablet keeps freezing in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freezes in time' reads as one phrase; 'in' is a piece and 'time' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is the time served learning a trade, as one serves one's time.
